text.p: selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Doctors' deal could cost $1-billion: Health Minister says increase in billing levels needed to serve aging population.
- Manning condemns convict vote: Talks tough in Bernardo riding.
- Private health centre slammed: Alberta proposal upsets Dingwall.
- Britain sets up vote on transfer power: Labour moves to hold referendums on creation of assemblies in Scotland, Wales.
- Cuban dissident describes long road to jail: Recently freed writer, now making his home in Canada, says he went from a dreamy-eyed supporter of Fidel Castro t one of the disenchanted.
- Thiessen sparks dollar rally: Currency jumps to US$O.7297 after central bank chief switches gears on interest rate hikes.
- Cambridge plans to sell Toronto site: Cash to finance Markborough takeover.
- Southam profit leaps in first quarter: Cites acquisitions, lower newsprint costs.
- Funds buck stock scare in April: $2.7-billion invested despite market volatility early in month.

- C$ surges on rate outlook: Central bank governor Gordon Thiessen says gross domestic product is set to expand at a rate of about 4% a year and low interest rates are no longer needed to prop up economy.
- Placer faces US$270M claim in Kazakh feud.
